description:
Convert the example ping extension and Interactive's slash-command dispatch to use the UI behaviour explicitly. Remove the convenience path where a handler's return value was used as a notification.

## Deliverable

ping.ex calls OctoPi.Coder.Extension.UI.notify(ctx.ui, "pong!") inside its handler. Interactive's notify_extension_result/2, run_extension_command/3, and {:extension_result, _} loop handler are deleted. Slash command invocation is unified with event flow — the Runner dispatches to registered command handlers, not a parallel Task.

## Steps

STEP 1 — Update .octo_pi/extensions/ping.ex to use UI.notify(ctx.ui, "pong!") in its handler. Handler returns :ok or whatever the new contract requires; not a notification string.

STEP 2 — Delete from interactive.ex:
  - notify_extension_result/2 (interactive.ex:1157-1164)
  - run_extension_command/3 (interactive.ex:1144-1155)
  - The {:extension_result, _} clause in handle_loop_msg (interactive.ex:633)

STEP 3 — Wire slash command invocation through the Runner: when Interactive sees a /name submission, send `{:invoke_command, name, args}` to Session (or directly to Runner via Session.get_runner); Runner looks up the registered command handler and calls it. Command handler runs in the same dispatch path as event handlers — no separate Task in Interactive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ping.ex source contains UI.notify(ctx.ui, ...) and does NOT return a notification string
- [ ] `grep -n "notify_extension_result\|run_extension_command\|:extension_result" apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex` returns 0 matches
- [ ] When `mix pi` runs and user types `/ping<Enter>`, "pong!" appears via the UI notification path (state.notification set, re-render fires)
- [ ] TUI integration test: submit `/ping`, assert notification visible. NO Process.sleep.
- [ ] mix test passes

## Dependencies
